This page documents my use of generative AI for the
[Class 3 note](class3.qmd).

## Tool Information

| Item | Details |
|---|---|
| **Tool** | Claude (Anthropic), model `claude-opus-5`, used in the Claude desktop app |
| **Date** | September 23, 2026 |
| **Language** | I worked in Traditional Chinese and asked for an English version of the finished note. |

## How the Note Was Produced

I watched *Journalism in the Age of Data* and read the accompanying site, then
dictated my points to Claude, which organised them into the Chinese note and
then into the English version published here.

**The content is mine.** These were the points I brought out of the video:

- Many Eyes and IBM's push to **democratise visualization** — and my reservation
  that an easy tool does not make data easy to interpret.
- The **Martini Glass** structure, and the worked example of how I would stage an
  interactive unemployment chart: trend and definitions first, comparison after.
- The **streamgraph of box-office revenues** as a case where visual appeal and
  readability pull apart.
- The conclusion I wanted to reach: a chart should be judged by the **task** it
  supports — compare, follow a trend, read a distribution — not by how novel it
  looks.

**What Claude contributed:** the ordering of the paragraphs, the transitions, and
the English wording. The draft structure is the model's; the observations and the
judgements in it are mine.

## Reading Support

Separately, I asked Claude to produce a Traditional Chinese reading guide to
chapters 1–3 of Ware's *Information Visualization*, to get through the assigned
reading faster in a second language. That guide is a study aid kept in my course
folder; it is not part of any submitted work, and nothing from it was copied into
the note above.

## Why I Used AI Here

English is not my first language and the note was due in the same week as work
for two other courses. Using AI to draft from my own points let me spend the time
on the video and the reading rather than on sentence construction.
